issues.location: Evidence room #ev-xl, the quote reader #xrPair (aria-live=polite), both columns, in Then, Now and Both
issues.problem: Removed or added tokens are hidden only with font-size:0 (span.x, computed width 0, opacity 1, visibility visible). They stay in the accessibility tree, and #xrPair is a polite live region. A screen reader therefore reads a mix of both versions, and reads it again on every mode or language change. Playwright ariaSnapshot of 'Now · Oct 2026' for Arabic Gaza genocide gives: 'Israel has been accusedThe genocide of committing crimesGaza is the systematic… during the Gaza war.between Israel and Hamas.' The Arabic paragraph is merged the same way ('…ضد الشعبالإبادة الجماعية لغزة…'). On a page where quotes must be exact, a blind reader hears a misquote.
issues.fix:
Keep the morph look, but remove inactive tokens from the accessibility tree. Once the animation ends, give every token that is not part of the shown state aria-hidden="true" (and inert). During the morph, set aria-busy="true" on #xrPair. Better still, take aria-live off #xrPair and add a visually hidden

that receives one clean string after each change: 'Arabic, Gaza genocide, October 2026: . Our translation: .' In Both, put a visually hidden 'removed:' or 'added:' before each or run. Apply the same treatment to #brS in #breathe, which uses the same diff rendering.

issues.location: Evidence room #ev-oct7 on phone (iPhone 13), after following the story's #oct7 'See the evidence' link: #evBack banner against the docked #o7Ctl
issues.problem: When the reader arrives from the story, the #evBack banner (fixed, 612–652px) sits on top of the docked step control #o7Ctl ('zi-ctl stuck', 590–656px). elementFromPoint at the centre of '‹ Prev' (x 51, y 614) returns DIV#evBack. The same happens wherever a docked sheet meets the banner (#netDet in #ev-organised).
issues.fix: Stack them instead of overlapping them. When #evBack is visible, set --dock-offset: <banner height + 8px> on body, and give .zi-ctl.stuck and .net-det.docked bottom: var(--dock-offset, 0). An alternative is to fold the banner into the dock row as a compact '← story' button at the left of #o7Ctl while the dock is stuck. Check on phone that '‹ Prev' gets the tap after arriving from #oct7.

issues.location: #organised story network #net and its detail sheet #netDet (edges and nodes, desktop and phone)
issues.problem: Round-6 fix 5 was not done. A selected edge still reads 'A4 – A1: shared 5 articles; chance gives 1.3 (95% of rewired worlds ≤ 3); p 0.001; same direction 80%', which a lay reader cannot follow. issues.location: Phone landings in the Evidence room: #charge 'See the evidence' → #ppFig, and #oct7 'See the evidence' → #o7T

reviews.notes:
I tested everything with Playwright on the shared build r7_shared_w.html, with iPhone 13 and 1280×900, and with reduced motion. My scripts and screenshots are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-photoStamper/bb344c8a-11d1-57c4-b6a1-fd224fa30cfd/scratchpad/qa/r7_ux/. I edited no repo files.

Round-6 fixes confirmed: #xmTip with hover, focus and tap; one Tab stop on the grid; phase row follows the playhead on phone; badges are real buttons; #o7Ctl docks at 66px on phone; #netDet docks only once the graph is on screen; the counter strip replaces the network tabs.

Round-6 UX items still open: the jargon in the edge detail text (issue 3), phone landings hidden under the tab bar (issue 4), the swipe hint (issue 8), the lab deep link and banner (issue 11), and the inline RTL gloss chips in #xrPair (the 'the genocide' chip still sits between الإبادة الجماعية and لغزة).

#breathe's 420ms 'A wording that was undone' flash during a drag is intended (brMove), not a bug.

Two things outside the UX lens that the orchestrator should know:
1. The Evidence room bottom line in #ev-organised (#orgH, page_template.html line 1706) still says ArbCom 'sanctioned editors for off-wiki canvassing on both sides of this subject; we could not open its case pages to check'. Line 1720 and the hatched-window caption near line 4234 say the same 'not checked against the case pages'. Must-fix 10 says to drop 'on both sides' everywhere and cite the PIA5 primary pages. Round 6 lists the primary-page check as the remaining publication blocker for #organised, and the story link text still says '(not verified)'.
2. The shared screenshot harness r7_shots.js switches tabs with '[role=tab]', but the page has no role=tab elements; the view links are a#tabReport, a#tabEv, a#tabLab with aria-current. So every 'evidence_*' screenshot is a copy of the story view (desk_dark_story_organised.png and desk_dark_evidence_organised.png have identical md5), no Evidence-room section was captured, and the second half of r7_text.txt repeats the story text. Other lenses that relied on those files have not seen the Evidence room.

strengths: My desk would run this, as a weekend online lead plus a 90-second evening-news segment headed 'how the world reads us'. The first phone screen (H1 at y=159 to 290, dek ends at y=707 on a 390x844 screen) carries the exact Israel genocide quote with its date (since 4 May 2025) and 'Israel's denial follows', so the lead fact can be checked before the first scroll. I confirmed the 4.6M views (4,617,834, mass2/cards.md:137) and the 7-of-150 split (PERP.md card 2).

Round-6 newsroom fixes landed and are visible: the sexual-violence pair is now in the #oct7 deck ('Israel and international media have reported rape and sexual assault by Hamas fighters' vs 'Numerous sources have reported dozens of cases of rape and sexual assault,' naming no perpetrator). Hamas's then/now definition is shown. The #oct7 bottom line now separates the opening section from the first sentence. The blue square appears on both October 2026 rows. The #against settlement item is correct.

Section H2s lead with the narrative and use Wikipedia as the vessel. #zionism, #charge and #palestine each pair an exact then-quote with an exact now-quote, and every one can be checked in its own section. #palestine has the best bottom line on the page: it names who is blamed, notes the asymmetry ('For the Jews who "fled or were expelled from Arab states," no one is named') and uses no statistic.

The page is highly quotable, and each line is verifiable on screen. 'After the Hamas-led October 7 attacks, Israel began committing genocide against Palestinians in Gaza.' / 'Netanyahu's government has been orchestrating the Gaza genocide' (NO DENIAL) / 'Hamas's terror designation moved from sentence 5 to sentence 22' / 'The Nakba … is the ethnic cleansing of Palestinian Arabs by Zionists' / Spanish: October 7 was 'un ataque de represalia' (verified in langs/LANGS.md:11).

The calibration protects the story on air. 'THE 2021 VERSION ALSO TOOK A POSITION' on the Nakba card, the Exploratory tag on #crosslang, 'Timing does not prove cause', 'may be reverted' on the 31 Oct Hamas copy and the October 7 genocide-clause removal, the honest #trust line (no larger than other conflicts across all 49,000 pages), and the adder-remover split in #organised all give a presenter answers to the obvious hostile questions.

issues.location: Hero H1 (h1, page_template.html hero): 'In 2021, Wikipedia spoke of “re-establishment.” Now it says “colonization” and “genocide.”'
issues.problem: (1) The H1 has no subject. A viewer cannot tell what was being 're-established' or what is 'colonization'; the headline only works if you already know the Zionism story. (2) It is a compressed copy of the #zionism H2, one screen below, which the owner asked not to repeat (MUSTFIX_owner §8). (3) Its grammatical subject is Wikipedia, not Israel's story (ANGLE.md, 8 Nov). (4) 'In 2021' is soft: 're-establishment' left in June 2021, as the #zionism body says. The H1 also runs to 4 lines on a 390px phone, against the owner's cap of 3. Round 6 deferred this as the editor's pick. From a news desk, it is still the weakest headline on the page.
issues.fix: H1 (12 words, 3 phone lines): 'Colonization, ethnic cleansing, genocide: the words Wikipedia now uses for Israel’s story.' Each word is anchored in the dek: Zionism 'through colonization', the Nakba 'ethnic cleansing … by Zionists', Israel 'began committing genocide'. If the editor insists on the then/now shape, use one that does not reuse the Zionism pair: 'Before the war, no leading Wikipedia article accused Israel of genocide. Now Israel’s own article does.' In that case, add 'None of the 150 most-read articles on the subject made the charge before the war.' as the dek's second sentence.

issues.location: Hero published line ('Published 8 November 2026 · … AI readers coded some sentences…'); no byline anywhere
issues.problem: There is still no author, organisation or contact (open since round 5). Without a name, 'AI readers coded some sentences' invites the 'bots wrote it' attack. No Israeli channel can credit or book the piece without a name.
issues.fix: Add under the dek: 'By [name / organisation] · [email]. Every quote and date was checked against the stored revision; automated readers coded the direction of some edits, and we hand-checked a sample (see How far to trust this).' Do not publish without a real name.

issues.location: #organised story link ('…what Wikipedia’s Arbitration Committee is reported to have found (not verified)'), #ev-organised bottom line (page_template.html:1706), #orgRec caption (:1720)
issues.problem: MUSTFIX_owner §10 has not landed. The evidence room still says ArbCom sanctioned editors 'on both sides' and that 'we could not open its case pages'. But guard/arbcom.md now holds the primary PIA4/PIA5 pages, and they record a ban 'for off-wiki misconduct relating to the PIA topic area' (9 Dec 2024) with no side stated. A hostile media-watch site that reads the case page will catch 'both sides' and 'could not open' as false. The strongest new organised-editing result, the talk-page voting blocs (guard/cards.md card 3), is missing from the story.
issues.fix: Bottom line of #ev-organised: 'Wikipedia’s Arbitration Committee banned an editor on 9 December 2024 “for off-wiki misconduct relating to the PIA topic area”; its decision does not say which side. Press reports of a pro-Palestinian Discord channel and pro-Israel email canvassing are listed below as reported.' Drop 'on both sides' everywhere. Change the story link to '…and what Wikipedia’s Arbitration Committee decided.' Add one sentence to the #organised deck: 'On talk-page votes, four groups of three to six accounts voted together 89 to 100% of the time, against about half by chance: camp voting, not proof of off-wiki coordination.' (guard/cards.md card 3; direction not coded, so name no side.)

issues.location: Hero dek, last sentence ('The hostages have never been in October 7’s first sentence.') and the Zionism clause ('has been “a Jewish homeland through colonization” since 27 August 2026')
issues.problem: (a) The dek uses the weakest true hostage fact. First sentences rarely carry tolls, and #oct7 then says the opening section does name the hostages, so the hero line reads as a gotcha. The stronger fact, for both newsworthiness and defensibility, is that the Israel and Hamas openings never mention them. (b) 'Since 27 August 2026' suggests 'colonization' is new. In fact 'colonial' or 'colonization' has been in the sentence on 99 to 100% of days since 5 June 2024 (stepper phases 2 and 3). A critic who checks January 2025 will find 'colonial' and say the date is wrong.
issues.fix: (a) 'The opening sections of the Israel and Hamas articles do not mention the hostages, and October 7’s first sentence never has.' (Scope: OCT7.md §6, where both articles have 0 mentions in every copy including now.) (b) 'Zionism, the “re-establishment” of a Jewish state in January 2021, has been described with “colonial” or “colonization” almost every day since June 2024; the current “a Jewish homeland through colonization” has stood since 27 August 2026.'

issues.location: #oct7 H2 ('October 7 was “coordinated attacks.” Now it is “coordinated armed incursions.” The Israel and Hamas openings do not mention the hostages.')
issues.problem: It runs to 5 lines on phone and makes three claims. It leads with the weakest change, attacks to armed incursions, which a viewer may read as a synonym. The Israeli story is that the first sentence never kept 'massacre', 'terror' or the hostages, and that the hostages are missing from Israel and Hamas.
issues.fix: H2: 'Wikipedia’s first line on October 7 says “coordinated armed incursions.” Its articles on Israel and Hamas do not mention the hostages.' Bottom line (no numbers): 'October 7’s opening section describes the massacre and names the hostages, but its first sentence calls it only “armed incursions,” and Hamas’s terror designation now comes second to last in its own article.'

issues.location: #zionism bottom line
issues.problem: Two statistics ('nine in ten … six in ten'). The second sentence leads with mechanics ('Edits pushed both ways; … softening edits'), and 'six in ten critical ones' weakens the point without explaining it.
issues.fix: 'Wikipedia’s one-line answer to “What is Zionism?” no longer speaks of the “re-establishment” of a Jewish state; it says a Jewish homeland “through colonization.” Edits pushed both ways, but attempts to soften the sentence were undone faster: nine in ten within a day.' (64/70, zionism/CODES.md; the 47/78 figure stays in #ziCodes.)

issues.location: #against H2 and bottom line
issues.problem: 'The 1948 expulsion moved its expellers to the second sentence' is clumsy English and hard for a presenter to say. The bottom line leads with mechanics ('critical term taken out of topic opening paragraphs'), and 'topic' is internal jargon. The settlement item ends in a hardening inside a section headed 'THE OTHER DIRECTION' without a label.
issues.fix: H2: 'Some lines moved Israel’s way: October 7 lost a clause calling Israel’s response genocide, and the 1948 expulsion article took the expellers’ names out of its first sentence.' Bottom line: 'These are exceptions: for every loaded term removed from these opening paragraphs, almost four were added; on other conflicts’ pages, fewer than two.' Prefix the settlement item: 'Israeli settlement (softened in 2022, hardened again in November 2026).'

issues.location: #crosslang H2 ('…Hebrew’s Gaza war article cites only South Africa’s court case.')
issues.problem: For an Israeli audience the hook is Hebrew against English, and that sits only in the bottom line. The H2's Hebrew clause is technical, and it reintroduces the court case that the owner removed from the story (MUSTFIX §4). The bottom line then repeats the H2's three languages.
issues.fix: H2: 'Hebrew Wikipedia calls October 7 a massacre and Hamas a terror organisation. English does neither; Spanish, Portuguese and Arabic now state the genocide charge as fact.' Bottom line: 'German, French, Italian and Dutch, like Hebrew, call October 7 terror or a massacre in their own voice; on genocide, four of eleven editions now state it as fact, up from none.' WHAT I WOULD PUBLISH (verified page content only):
HEADLINE: 'Colonization, ethnic cleansing, genocide: the words Wikipedia now uses for Israel’s story'
DEK: 'English Wikipedia’s Israel article, viewed 4.6 million times in the past 12 months, now states in its own voice that after October 7 “Israel began committing genocide against Palestinians in Gaza.” Before the war, none of the 150 most-read articles on the subject made that charge. Zionism is now “a Jewish homeland through colonization,” and the Nakba “the ethnic cleansing of Palestinian Arabs by Zionists.” The articles on Israel and Hamas do not mention the hostages.'
P1: 'The genocide sentence sits in the opening section of the article on Israel and has stood since 4 May 2025; eight earlier insertions, from November 2023 on, did not last. The next sentence reads: “Israel has denied that its actions constitute genocide.” The article on Benjamin Netanyahu carries the charge with no denial: “Netanyahu's government has been orchestrating the Gaza genocide.” Five more of the most-read articles (Palestine, Gaza Strip, Israeli–Palestinian conflict, Israel Defense Forces and Gaza–Israel conflict) carry it but attribute it to others.'
P2: 'In January 2021, Wikipedia’s one-line answer to “What is Zionism?” spoke of “the re-establishment of and support for a Jewish state in the territory defined as the historic Land of Israel.” “Re-establishment” left for good on 9 July 2024. “Colonial” first went in on 5 June 2024 and went in and out 33 and 32 times in six months; the current “a Jewish homeland through colonization” has stood since 27 August 2026. The sentence was changed 292 times. Edits pushed both ways, but attempts to soften it were undone faster: nine in ten within a day.'
P3: 'October 7’s first sentence calls the attack “a series of coordinated armed incursions … carried out by Hamas and several other Palestinian militant groups”; the opening section goes on to describe the massacre and name the hostages. Its line on sexual violence once read “reported rape and sexual assault by Hamas fighters”; it now names no perpetrator. Hamas, “militant” in 2021, is now “a political organisation with a military wing,” and the sentence on its terror designation has moved from fifth to second-to-last. In the 1948 articles, Wikipedia now says in its own voice who drove the Palestinians out, “Zionists” or “Zionist forces”; for the Jews who “fled or were expelled from Arab states,” no one is named.'
(The fourth paragraph must carry the calibration: some lines moved Israel’s way, almost four loaded terms were added for every one removed, and across all 49,000 pages the change is no larger than in other conflicts.)

NARRATIVE vs MECHANICS: #zionism, #charge, #palestine and #oct7 lead with the narrative. #after leads with a word game, #against and #trust lead with mechanics, and #organised necessarily does too. The hero H1 makes Wikipedia, not Israel's story, the subject; that is the main gap.

issues.problem: Both critics can hit the first line. (1) 'Wikipedia spoke of' generalises one clause in one article (Zionism) to the whole encyclopedia. (2) The H1 joins two articles: 're-establishment' is Zionism, 'genocide' is Israel. (3) 're-establishment' was in the sentence only from 1 Jan to 7 Jun 2021, plus two weeks in 2024. issues.location: #after H2 (l.1370 'Other definitions moved after later battles'), bottom line (l.1371 'changed within weeks of a battle'), deck (l.1372 'Events were frequent: the three weeks after one on our calendar cover two in five weeks')
issues.problem: The section still implies that battles drove the wording, against its own numbers. The windows cover 40.6% of all weeks (data/event_timing_mass2.json weeks_share 0.406), so 'within weeks of a battle' is close to guaranteed for any edit. Three of the five cards say so in their own stat lines: ground war 8.7 vs 8.3 (no clear rise), May 2025 2.0 vs 2.2 (fewer), ceasefire 3.0 vs 2.7 (no clear rise). Yet each card opens by tying a wording change to a battle ('a week after the fighting resumed', 'ten days into the May offensive'). Only October 7 (3.8→13.7) and Rafah (4.7→7.3) show a rise. The deck sentence is also garbled.

Bottom line: 'New critical terms more than tripled in the three weeks after October 7 and rose after Rafah; other battles brought no clear rise. Today’s definitions of Hamas, October 7, the Nakba, Zionism and the Gaza war were mostly set later.' Deck: 'Battles and escalations were so frequent that two in every five weeks fell within three weeks of one, so a change landing after a battle gives a date, not a cause.' In cards 2 and 4, open with the date and the edit, then the event.

issues.location: #organised counter strip ('14 linked pairs found · about 2 expected by chance · comparison articles: 3') and bottom line l.1428 'on comparison articles, none did'
issues.problem: The counter can be read wrong in both directions. Comparison articles had almost the same volume (1,586 critical-term edits by 847 accounts vs 1,620 by 697; coord/chart_data/network.json counts), and their 3 links vs 0.28 by chance is about 11 times chance, against about 6.5 times for topic (14 vs 2.15). The hit-piece critic: beyond-chance co-editing is ordinary Wikipedia, and the page implies something sinister. The whitewash critic: on equal volume the topic area has nearly five times as many linked pairs, and the page doesn't say so. Separately, 'none did' on comparison key articles has no denominator (WHO.md card 8 gives 216 traced changes for topic, none for comparison), so a reader can't tell whether those pages had any first-sentence changes to share.
issues.fix: Counter line: 'Topic articles: 14 linked pairs, about 6 times chance (2.1). Comparison articles, with as many edits: 3, also above chance (0.28). Regulars cluster on every contested page; this subject has more of them.' Bottom line: add the comparison denominator from coordination.lead_authors ('… on the N comparison key articles, whose first sentences changed M times, no account did'). If M is small, drop the contrast.

issues.location: #zionism bottom line (l.1295) 'Edits pushed both ways; nine in ten softening edits were gone within a day, six in ten critical ones.'
issues.problem: This is a balance claim with no proportion, and it widens the scope. The 64/70 and 47/78 figures cover only the 148 changes coded as setting a disputed description in Wikipedia's own voice (CODES.md headline cell), not the 292 edits in the section kicker. 'Softening' is not the codebook's term ('less critical'). The proportion (78 vs 70) appears only under the chart. The whitewash critic will read 'nine in ten gone within a day' as proof of guarding, but the site-wide revert test found that removals of critical terms were not reverted faster (median 1.13 h vs 0.84 h, p 0.87; guard/cards.md card 1).
issues.fix: Bottom line: 'Wikipedia’s one-line answer to “What is Zionism?” no longer speaks of “re-establishment”; it says a homeland “through colonization.” Of the edits that set a disputed description in Wikipedia’s own voice, 78 made it more critical and 70 less, but 64 of the 70 were gone within a day, against 47 of the 78.' In #ev-zionism add one line: 'Across all 254 core articles, removals of critical terms were not reverted faster than additions.'

The hit-piece critic will screenshot it as 'Israeli study draws a ring around Wikipedia editors', even though the page's own test doesn't support the group.
issues.fix: In the story view, drop the hull for confidence === 'low' and draw its nodes and edges ungrouped and greyed. If the label stays, use 'Not beyond chance (low confidence)' in the muted ink. Keep the hull only in the #netEv evidence-room view, where the Groups table explains confidence.

issues.location: #against bottom line and data line ('Critical terms in opening paragraphs … topic, 223 in, 61 out'); list items 'October 7 attacks … That edit may be reverted' and 'Israeli settlement … On 4 November 2026 the first sentence hardened again'

Terror vocabulary moved the same way as the critical terms: down 24% in topic opening paragraphs, flat in comparison.' issues.location: #charge, under the Israel quote ('The next sentence: “Israel has denied that its actions constitute genocide.”', l.1337)

Don't add a comparator from memory: verify it against stored text.

Both critics will read it their own way: 'barely there' or 'up to 11 points'. The box also holds two population sentences where the owner asked for one (MUSTFIX 3).
